topic.title: The First Time You Translate a Project
topic.shortdesc: What to expect the very first time you run translation in a project.

body.p: The first time you run a translation job in a project, the agent has no existing translated content to reuse. As a result, it creates everything needed for the translated content:

ul.li: A translated publication, with a translated copy of every topic and map reachable from the source publication.

body.p: The agent also copies every binary resource referenced from the DITA map (for example images and other non-translatable files used by the publication), and creates the folders required by the project's default structure. See Choosing a Project Structure for Translation for details about how these folders are organized.

For each target language, the agent tries to reproduce the deliverables that already exist for the source language. This allows the translated publication to be built and published in the same way as the original. If you want a different set of deliverables for a target language, instruct the agent accordingly (see Customizing the Translation Behavior).

p.note: Because the first translation job sets up the project structure and conventions that later jobs will follow, it is best to start with a small publication. This gives you a chance to verify that the agent created the folders, translation index, and deliverables as expected before you translate the rest of your content.

body.p: The steps for starting a translation job, monitoring it, and reviewing the results are the same as for later jobs. See Following and Managing a Translation Job and the Getting Started with Translation walkthrough.
